title: Content capture, redaction and privacy
summary: Prompts, outputs and tool payloads are the best debugging evidence and the riskiest telemetry. The GenAI conventions make content capture opt-in, and production setups usually keep it off spans, in a governed store, referenced from the trace.
useIf: You decide whether and how telemetry may hold prompts, retrieved text and tool results.
avoidIf: You flip one global content flag in production without redaction, retention and access rules.

explain.md: The conventions say instrumentations SHOULD NOT capture content by default. The opt-in attributes are `gen_ai.system_instructions`, `gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, `gen_ai.tool.definitions`, `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` and `gen_ai.tool.call.result`. They describe three patterns: (1) record nothing, the default; (2) record content on spans, suited to pre-production or telemetry that meets your privacy rules; (3) store content externally and put **references** on spans, recommended for production. An in-process upload hook runs regardless of the span sampling decision and independent of the opt-in flags, and the spec still lists TODO for a common reference format [[r4]].

Agent Framework's switch is `ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA` (default false) in Python and `EnableSensitiveData` in .NET. Sensitive data means prompts, responses, tool arguments and tool results. In workflows it also controls `executor.input`, `executor.output` and `message.content` [[r10]] [[r11]]. Foundry and the Azure SDKs use `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true`, and the older classic page used `AZURE_TRACING_GEN_AI_CONTENT_RECORDING_ENABLED`. The `@trace_function` decorator always records parameters and return values regardless of that flag [[r13]].

explain.takeaway: Default to shape only. Move content to a governed store when you must read it, and capture on spans only for data you may freely keep.

whereToUse: Pre-production debugging with synthetic prompts and full content on spans
Production assistants over personal or confidential data, where content is stored by reference
Evaluation pipelines that score sampled conversations and need the text under controls
Incident review where a restricted group may open a specific conversation
Policy documents that state what telemetry may hold and for how long

use: Keep content off by default and enable it per environment and per purpose
Store production content externally with references on spans, short retention and role-based access
Redact known identifiers before anything leaves the process, and test the redaction
avoid: Do not enable content capture globally in production because it was needed once
Do not forget that decorators such as `@trace_function` record arguments regardless of the flag
Do not let operations staff and data owners share one access role
flips: Regulation forbids storing content: keep shape only and reproduce issues with synthetic inputs
Support must reproduce wrong answers: add a break-glass path that retrieves the stored conversation for one ticket
You use a hosted backend you do not control: assume content on spans is visible to the vendor and decide accordingly

pitfalls.symptom: Prompts show up in Application Insights although sensitive data is off
pitfalls.cause: A `@trace_function` decorated function records its parameters and return values regardless of the flag
pitfalls.fix: Remove the decorator from sensitive paths or redact arguments before the call [[r13]]

pitfalls.symptom: Prompts and outputs appear twice on parent and child spans in .NET
pitfalls.cause: Both the chat client and the agent were instrumented with sensitive data on

scenarios.title: A pre-production agent with synthetic data
scenarios.situation: A team builds an agent and tests it with synthetic prompts. They want to read full prompts and tool results while tuning behavior. Telemetry goes to a development backend.
unknowns: Could real data reach this environment later?
Who can read the dev backend?
scenarios.question: What content policy do you set?

options.name: Content on spans, enabled only in the development environment
options.why: No privacy cost and the fastest debugging.
options.tradeoff: The setting must not be copied to production.

options.name: Metadata only
options.tradeoff: Slows tuning because you cannot read prompts.

options.name: External store with references
options.why: It adds a storage system and access flow with no data sensitivity to justify it.
options.tradeoff: Right once real user data appears.

flips.if: Real user prompts reach the environment
flips.then: Move to external storage or metadata only.

flips.if: The dev backend is shared widely
flips.then: Restrict who can read content attributes.

scenarios.takeaway: Capture freely only where the data is yours to share.

scenarios.title: Production over regulated records with a support team
scenarios.situation: A production assistant handles confidential case records. Support needs to reproduce a wrong answer for a specific ticket. Auditors require retention limits and access logs.
unknowns: Who may open a stored conversation?
How long must content be retained?
scenarios.question: How do you capture content?

options.name: External content store with references on spans, short retention, role-based access and audit logs
options.why: Traces carry ids only, and authorized people retrieve content for one ticket under logged access.
options.tradeoff: You build and run another governed store.

options.name: Content on spans in the shared telemetry backend
options.why: Many engineers can read it and retention follows the telemetry store, not the data rules.

options.name: Metadata only and ask users to resend inputs
options.tradeoff: Slow, unreliable reproduction and poor user experience.

flips.if: No content may be stored at all
flips.then: Use metadata only and synthetic reproduction.

flips.if: Only a few conversations per month need review
flips.then: Capture content only for flagged or failed runs.

scenarios.takeaway: Separate who sees run shape from who sees user content.

quiz.q: Which pattern do the GenAI conventions recommend for production?
options: Store content externally and put references on spans
Record content only on the root span
quiz.explain: The conventions list three patterns and recommend external storage with references for production. Content on spans suits pre-production or telemetry that meets privacy rules.

quiz.q: Match each switch to the layer it controls.

pairs.r: OTel and Azure SDK message content
Always records parameters and return values

quiz.explain: Three similar flags exist for three layers, and the decorator records arguments regardless of any of them.

quiz.q: Sensitive data is off in Agent Framework, but a tool argument containing a customer id appears in traces. What is the likeliest cause?
options: A `@trace_function` decorator on that function records parameters and returns regardless of the flag
The model logs its own prompts
quiz.explain: The decorator always records parameters and return values. The backend cannot change what the process exports, sampling affects volume not content, and the model does not write your telemetry.

flashcards.front: What is the default for content capture in the GenAI conventions?
flashcards.back: Off. Instrumentations SHOULD NOT capture content by default. The content attributes are opt-in.

flashcards.front: Which content pattern is recommended for production?
flashcards.back: Store content externally and record references on spans. Content on spans suits pre-production or data you may freely keep.
The sensitive-data flag. It always records parameters and return values.
